title: feat(runtime): a sandboxed body can do time-zone date maths, through Intl.DateTimeFormat
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-project-manager"} -->
_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X5pePkMPaas25B8dVLe6RiN)_

Fixes #28898

Clause-②: no
No published schema, type, export or error code moves. The one `packages/spec` change is the job `handler` key's `.describe()` text (and the reference page regenerated from it); the accept set is identical. The sandbox's globals are not declared by any spec schema: `ScriptBodySchema.source` is a string, and what it may call is the runtime's answer, which is what changes here.

Metadata-protocol: none
What a metadata author can write is unchanged: no key, value, type or default moves. A body `source` that calls `Intl.DateTimeFormat` was already accepted at every door; it now runs instead of throwing `ReferenceError`.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:沙箱(QuickJS)里有了 `Intl.DateTimeFormat`,完整的一整个构造器(`format`/`formatToParts`/`formatRange`/`formatRangeToParts`/`resolvedOptions`/`supportedLocalesOf`),结果由服务器自己的 `Intl` 算出,所以 IANA 时区和夏令时边界与服务器一致。`Intl` 的其它成员都不存在。钩子、动作、作业三种 body 共用同一个 runner,所以三者同时获得。`os build` 的降级判断随之按成员判:只用 `Intl.DateTimeFormat` 的 handler 现在能降级成 body,用 `Intl.NumberFormat` 等仍打包。作业 `handler` 的弃用说明补了一句"时区日期计算可用 `Intl.DateTimeFormat` 迁到 `body`"。
- 为什么改:duly#147 的派单作业要按每个职责自己的时区算当前周期,沙箱没有 `Intl`,作业就离不开已弃用的 `handler`。席位裁定走纯运行时路线,不给 `ctx` 加日期助手,作业上下文契约不动。
- 风险与回滚:跨边界只有纯值(一个 JSON 字符串 + 最多两个毫秒数进,一个 JSON 字符串出,在沙箱内解析),桥是闭包参数而非全局,"现在"取沙箱自己的 `Date.now()`,无新 I/O。回滚即 revert,无数据迁移。
- 先看:`packages/runtime/src/sandbox/sandbox-intl.ts`(垫片与宿主侧的值清洗、错误转译);`packages/cli/src/utils/detect-free-identifiers.ts` 的 `MEMBER_JUDGED_GLOBALS` 与 `collectReferences` 的成员分支;`packages/cli/src/utils/sandbox-globals-probe.test.ts` 的点号探针。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run src/sandbox/sandbox-intl.test.ts`,预期 `Tests 12 passed (12)`。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

- **`packages/runtime/src/sandbox/sandbox-intl.ts`** (new): `installSandboxIntl(vm)` installs `globalThis.Intl` (non-enumerable, like the built-in) with one member, `DateTimeFormat`: callable with or without `new`, `supportedLocalesOf`, and the whole prototype (`format` as a bound getter, `formatToParts`, `formatRange`, `formatRangeToParts`, `resolvedOptions`, `Symbol.toStringTag`). The VM-side constructor keeps only a plain-value snapshot of `locales` and of the option keys `DateTimeFormat` reads; every call asks the host to answer with a host `Intl.DateTimeFormat` built from that snapshot (a per-invocation cache of at most 64 formatters, dropped with the VM).
  - In: an op name, ONE JSON string, at most two numbers. The host re-reads the JSON and keeps only the known option keys with primitive values.
  - Out: one JSON string, parsed inside the VM, so `resolvedOptions()` and the parts arrays are VM objects. A host error becomes a VM `RangeError` / `TypeError` with the host's message: the body's own throw, never a host refusal relayed.
  - The bridge is a closure argument of the shim (no global), and the shim captures `JSON`, `Date.now` and friends at install, so a body replacing them cannot steer the host. `format()` with no argument takes "now" from the VM's own clock.
- **`packages/runtime/src/sandbox/quickjs-runner.ts`**: `execute()` calls `installSandboxIntl(vm)` right after `installCtx`. Every body kind (hook, action, job, and the L1 expression path) goes through `execute()`, so this is one seam and one global set.
- **`packages/cli/src/utils/detect-free-identifiers.ts`**: the measured allowlist learns member granularity. New `MEMBER_JUDGED_GLOBALS = {'Intl'}`; `collectReferences` records a non-computed `Intl.NAME` read as `Intl.NAME`; `SANDBOX_GLOBALS` gains `Intl.DateTimeFormat`; `NODE_ONLY_GLOBALS` swaps `Intl` for the ten other `Intl` members Node 22 has. A bare `Intl` use (`const I = Intl`, `Intl[k]`) or an unlisted member is reported host-only, so that handler stays bundled (the safe direction). A local or parameter named `Intl` still binds it.
- **`packages/cli/src/utils/extract-hook-body.ts`**: the host-only refusal sentence says "of `Intl` it provides `Intl.DateTimeFormat` only" when an `Intl` name is refused, and "would throw" where it said "would throw ReferenceError" (a missing member throws `TypeError`).
- **`packages/spec/src/system/job.zod.ts`**: the `handler` docblock and `.describe()` (the deprecation message) say time-zone date maths moves to `body` through `Intl.DateTimeFormat`. `content/docs/references/system/job.mdx` regenerated (`gen:schema && gen:docs`).
- **`content/docs/automation/jobs.mdx`**: one bullet under "What running in the sandbox means": `Intl.DateTimeFormat` is there whole, nothing else of `Intl` is, the feature test, and that hook and action bodies share it.
- **`.changeset/28898-sandbox-intl-date-time-format.md`**: `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/spec` patch; both declaration lines.

## Tests

- New `packages/runtime/src/sandbox/sandbox-intl.test.ts` (12, real QuickJS). Every expected value is computed with the host's `Intl` in the test, never a literal (CI's ICU differs from a container's).
  - The card reproduction: `formatToParts` of two instants either side of New York's 2026-03-08 spring-forward, in `America/New_York` and `Asia/Shanghai`, equals the host's (anti-vacuity: the zone name changes in New York and not in Shanghai).
  - `format`, `resolvedOptions`, `formatRange`, `formatRangeToParts` equal the host's; the period-start shape (calendar date of one instant in two zones: `2026-03-08` vs `2026-03-09`); callable without `new`, bound `format` getter, `instanceof`, both `toStringTag`s, `supportedLocalesOf`; options read at construction.
  - Errors: an invalid `timeZone` throws the host's `RangeError` text as a VM `RangeError` (and uncaught, fails the run with that text); `format(NaN)`, `formatRange(0)`, `formatToParts('not a date')` throw what the host throws.
  - Absent, not half-working: `Object.getOwnPropertyNames(Intl)` is `['DateTimeFormat']`, `typeof Intl.NumberFormat` is `'undefined'`, `Intl` is not enumerable.
  - Isolation: answers are VM-made (`Object.prototype` / `Array.prototype`), fresh per call; no global named like the bridge; a foreign receiver throws `TypeError`; replacing `JSON.stringify` / `Date.now` steers nothing.
  - One seam: a hook body and an action body answer the same. Through the job door: a `jobBodyRunnerFactory` job reports `period 2026-03-09`.
- New `packages/qa/dogfood/test/job-body-time-zone-date.dogfood.test.ts` (1): a booted stack declares a job whose `body` inserts each zone's calendar date of one instant; the job service triggers it, and `GET /data/tzj_period` reads both zones' own dates (anti-vacuity: the two dates differ; the job is listed as scheduled first).
- cli: `detect-free-identifiers.test.ts` (+3: `Intl.DateTimeFormat` has no free name; the bare namespace is reported; an unlisted member is reported), `extract-hook-body.test.ts` (+1: a handler using `Intl.DateTimeFormat` lowers), `hook-body-lowering.test.ts` (+1: no finding for it), `sandbox-globals-probe.test.ts` (dotted names probed as namespace-then-member; +1: every member-judged namespace measures present and owns every dotted member). The #14301 refusal pins move from `Intl.DateTimeFormat` to `Intl.NumberFormat`, a member the sandbox still lacks, so the class stays pinned.

<details><summary>Red first, green, ablations</summary>

- Red on base `a3640933` (new runtime test, unchanged source): `Tests 12 failed (12)`, each `ReferenceError: 'Intl' is not defined` (the hook case: `hook 't' threw: ReferenceError: 'Intl' is not defined`).
- Green: `src/sandbox/` `Test Files 35 passed (35)`, `Tests 341 passed (341)`.
- Ablation, runtime (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, anchor `installSandboxIntl(vm);` hit once, blob `f779c2c2` to `8af3c789`; the test imports `src`): `Test Files 1 failed | 34 passed (35)`, `Tests 12 failed | 329 passed (341)`: exactly the 12 Intl cases. Restored: blob `f779c2c2` == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- Ablation, cli (anchor `'Intl.DateTimeFormat',` deleted from `SANDBOX_GLOBALS`, the four files, all `src`): `Tests 4 failed | 136 passed (140)`: the three new lower-it pins and the named-cases pin. The partition pin stays green, as it must: a name removed from a set is no longer probed, which is why the named-cases pin exists. Restored: blob `7df744bf` == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- Dogfood, red leg on a rebuilt dist (call replaced by `void installSandboxIntl;`, blob `f779c2c2` to `a8815ee9`; `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime build`; `ablation-dist-preflight` "marker absent from all 12 built files"): `Tests 1 failed (1)`, the job logged `job 'tzj_period_stamp' threw: ReferenceError: 'Intl' is not defined` and the read was `{}`. Restored: blob == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty; restore leg rebuilt, preflight "marker present in 2 built files", "working tree clean against HEAD", `Tests 1 passed (1)`.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- **Hook and action bodies share the runner** (measured: every production call site of `hookBodyRunnerFactory`, `actionBodyRunnerFactory` and `jobBodyRunnerFactory`, in `app-plugin.ts` and `app-artifact-handlers.ts`, hands the body to a `QuickJSScriptRunner`, one class in separate instances, and `QuickJSScriptRunner.execute()` is the only place a VM is made; `git grep "new QuickJSScriptRunner"` outside tests: 5 hits, all those factories), so they get the same `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, as the order rules. The L1 expression path goes through `execute()` too.
- **Why the cli moved in this PR.** `sandbox-globals-probe.test.ts` measures the sandbox's globals against the lowering allowlist, so the runtime change alone reds it (`Intl` measures present). Moving `Intl` wholesale to the sandbox set would have lowered a handler using `Intl.NumberFormat` into a body that throws, the #14301 failure class; leaving it host-only would keep printing "Intl is not provided by the sandbox", which this change makes false. Judging per member is the smallest honest change, and it is why `DateTimeFormat` is whole: a lowered handler calling `formatRange` must not throw where the in-process one works.
- **Published value change (cli `hook-body` subpath).** `HookBodyExtractionError.freeIdentifiers` / `nodeOnlyIdentifiers` now name the member (`Intl.NumberFormat`) where they named `Intl`; the error's shape and members are unchanged (`published-subpath-hook-body.pin.test.ts` green). The refusal sentence's host-only branch changed as listed above; the module-scope sentence the docs quote is byte-identical (its pin is green).
- **What a body can learn.** `new Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions()` reports the server's default locale and time zone, which a body could not read before. Values, not objects; noted for the seat, not treated as a leak.
- **Not done, out of scope.** QuickJS's own `Date.prototype.toLocaleString(locale, { timeZone })` exists and ignores its arguments; a handler using it lowers today and formats in the server zone. Not changed here (not class a/b/c with a measured reach). Dedupe words: toLocaleString timeZone sandbox ignored.
- **Overlap.** Before opening: none of the 31 open PRs touches `packages/runtime/src/sandbox/**`, the four cli files, `system/job.zod.ts` or `automation/jobs.mdx` (file lists read per PR); search for `quickjs`, `sandbox`, `detect-free-identifiers`, `Intl`, `job body`, `hook body` among open PRs found no related one.
